content: The combination of statins and fibrates has not been shown to improve atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) outcomes and is generally not recommended for clinical use. Specifically, the concurrent use of statins with gemfibrozil is strongly discouraged due to the heightened risk of rhabdomyolysis, particularly in individuals with compromised renal function. Data from the ACCORD trial demonstrated no additional benefit in reducing ASCVD risk when using this combination therapy compared to statin monotherapy.
